SoM marks — region mode vs box mode

Set-of-Mark (arXiv 2310.11441) lists three mark types — mask, box, alphanumeric — and says the type should be "image-dependent to avoid any conflicts with the original image contents". Two modes follow from that:

  • region mode (natural images): the SAM segment at the marked point, overlaid at alpha 0.4 with a contour, the number at the distance-transform maximum inside the region — the paper's method verbatim (visualizer.py's (+2,−6) offset and font-size rule included).
  • box mode (GUI, documents, anything text-bearing): a translucent overlay makes words unreadable, so these get the paper's box form — an unfilled outline, with the number placed OUTSIDE it, at whichever of six candidate corners carries the least image content. No glyph is ever covered.

Left = region mode  |  Right = box mode. The opaque ring that earlier versions drew on the judged point does not exist in the paper and is gone from both.
